item.title: Meta, Google and TikTok sue to block California's ban on addictive feeds for minors
item.description: The companies filed separate First Amendment challenges to Assembly Bill 1709 and asked a federal court to stop Attorney General Rob Bonta enforcing the law, which takes effect in January 2027.

item.title: Ukraine's ammunition needs a European funding line
item.description: Congress votes the money, but one office decides whether it moves. Europe's governments budget as if that were guaranteed, and they should not.

item.title: Hoax bomb threats ground or divert at least seven planes across Europe in two days
item.description: Airlines hit include LOT, Scandinavian Airlines and Wizz Air, and the AP and Telegraph report one aircraft was escorted by the Italian Air Force. Osprey Flight Solutions says the hoaxes fit a pattern of hybrid attacks on critical infrastructure.

item.title: US to mediate Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi, Kremlin keeps Europe out
item.description: The Kremlin says the trilateral format bars European participation, while Zelensky insists Europe must be included. Brussels will host separate recovery talks a week earlier.

item.title: EU blacklists 1,569 Russian military suppliers in what Council calls largest round
item.description: The listings bring the total under the 2014 regime to nearly 4,600, with work on a further sanctions package continuing. Brussels says it will not follow Washington's easing of sanctions on Russian diesel.

item.title: Parliament to demand stronger cyber rules as Member States contest the Commission's Act
item.description: The 11 November resolution presses for resilience of critical infrastructure while the Council contests ENISA's role, definitions and high-risk supplier rules.

item.title: Commission clears JD.com's Ceconomy takeover with ten-year market-terms commitments
item.description: The approval closes the final regulatory hurdle. In August 2026 Beijing barred organisations and individuals from cooperating with the EU subsidy probe and later warned of countermeasures.

item.title: Parliament debates cyber resilience as member states fight for control of CSA 2
item.description: The Irish Presidency has tabled a compromise on who decides cyber security powers, with the debate set for Wednesday at 15:00. Parliament has already demanded sovereign cyber detection and response capabilities by wide majorities.

item.title: New York Times calls Brave a burglar and an AI fence in copyright lawsuit
item.description: The complaint says the browser's paywall blocker and News index distribute Times journalism without permission, and that Brave sells unlicensed material through its Search API to AI companies. Brave said separately that Anthropic used its Search API to train Claude 2.

item.title: North Korean hackers stole more than $6.3 billion from Binance, US agencies say
item.description: The FBI and Secret Service named the TraderTraitor group and urged firms to block its laundering wallets, while Pyongyang rejected the charge as absurd. The company says about $3 billion has been frozen on-chain and user funds will be covered in full.

item.title: Darmanin says a Mélenchon or Le Pen win would end the EU as it exists today
item.description: He warned both programmes are built on the end of this Europe and urged a pro-European candidate to use the presidency to turn Europe into a power.

item.title: Commission effectively backs Tusk, says judge crisis is for Warsaw
item.description: The Commission says appointing Constitutional Tribunal judges lies with the Sejm, citing a European court order not to block the new judges. President Nawrocki denounced the takeover of the Tribunal and swore in only two of the six.

item.title: North Korean hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, FBI and Secret Service say
item.description: Chainalysis and BleepingComputer say exchanges, stablecoin issuers and Arbitrum froze billions, including $3 billion by Binance, but the attacker still holds $2.4 billion beyond any issuer's reach. Pyongyang denies any role.

item.title: Parliament delegation praises Hungary's reforms but leaves Article 7 decision open
item.description: The delegation has no mandate to close the procedure opened in 2018, and the Council has one month to rule on lifting measures affecting 4.2 billion euros.

item.title: EU drops associate membership label for Canada after German objection
item.description: The 28 October statement instead offers 'ever closer association', with the terms to be defined by the 2027 summit. Germany broke the silence procedure to force the change before the Montreal summit, with Italy and France also objecting.

item.title: European allies fear a lame-duck Trump could cut US troops in Europe, diplomats say
item.description: The Pentagon has already cancelled a brigade rotation to Poland and announced up to 5,000 troop cuts, while Congress set a floor of 76,000 US forces in Europe.

item.title: Supermarket refrigeration hacked again across Europe three weeks after France
item.description: The Commissioner called the repeat attacks a deliberate attempt to disrupt the food supply. The vulnerabilities were flagged before the first attack.

item.title: Attal calls for a common primary as Le Pen leads the 2027 run-off polls
item.description: Ipsos puts Le Pen on 33.5% with Macron's 2022 base split across three candidates. Retailleau has rejected the idea, and Lisnard warns France must decide quickly.

item.title: Any renewed strike on Iran would be decided in Washington, and Europe holds no seat there
item.description: Whether, when and against what any renewed American strike on Iran happens turns on one man in Washington; Israel's pressing for it is reported and denied, Qatar mediates and Iran waits. No European capital or institution appears at any point of the chain that reports show deciding the question.

item.title: Netherlands proposes bill to ban addictive algorithms, with switch-off as penalty
item.description: The PvdA proposal covers social media, games, dating apps and chatbots, and eight parliaments back it. Brussels' own cases against TikTok and Meta remain unfinished.

item.title: Brussels blocks national social media age limits for 12 months pending EU-wide rules
item.description: The Commission's Kids Act sets 15 as the minimum age for opening an account across the EU, but Greece and Denmark say they will not wait. Austria will keep its own law ready to take effect when the standstill expires in July 2027.

item.title: Russia quits Europe's torture prevention treaty, ending detention monitoring in Russia
item.description: The withdrawal took effect one year after notification, and no independent body can now inspect Russian places of detention. The Council of Europe says the CPT will continue its work in the 46 remaining member states.

item.title: Sport court orders ice hockey federation to readmit Russia for 2027 worlds
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport found only substantiated security concerns can exclude athletes by nationality. Finland says Russian athletes will have no business coming to Finland, and the EU is weighing an entry ban for the Germany tournament.

item.title: Ukraine takes initiative on three fronts, ISW says, as Russian October losses hit record
item.description: Kyiv says more than 54,000 Russian soldiers were killed or seriously wounded in October, the highest toll since the 2022 invasion began. ISW says Ukraine seized the initiative in three directions and defeated Russia's northern pincer plan.

item.title: Coalition of the Willing holds first exercise in Poland from 9 to 22 November
item.description: RMF FM reports nearly 5,000 soldiers taking part, joined by British, French and limited German forces, to test the command and logistics systems needed to move troops across Europe. The United States is not taking part, and in July Russia's ambassador called the drills symbolic.

item.title: Hackers send false missile and nuclear alerts to Kyiv and all Russia in one night
item.description: Ukraine's Air Alert app and Russia's Emergency Ministry app were breached hours apart, and both governments restored their systems and denied any real threat. A previously unknown group, Hitcore, claimed the Ukrainian breach.

item.title: Two sanctions in one year, all against one broadcaster, are politics
item.description: The Media Authority warned, fined and threatened Ongehoord Nederland for a year before acting. When Zembla and BNNVARA broke the rules, it stayed silent, and that is what destroys a regulator.

item.title: Water cannon answers the riot. Only a budget answers the protest.
item.description: France and Germany met a generation's demands with 70,000 police and prosecutors' circulars, and nothing else. A state that can only repress, not respond, will keep repressing.

item.title: A union that outsources its border doesn't have one
item.description: The Council majority calls a bigger Frontex unnecessary while returns still depend on deals that can collapse with one election abroad. Build the 30,000-strong corps properly, write the safeguards in, and stop pretending the border works.

item.title: Poland's twenty-year EU ledger meets a budget that prices the border, not the balance
item.description: Poland enters the 2028-2034 budget talks with the union's strongest growth record and a fiscal bill of its own. The negotiating box measures it by Russia and Belarus instead, so the argument over what membership built is now the argument over what it gets.
